title: Just Got a 401(k)
for: HR handed you a form with fund names on it and you don't know what any of them mean.

stops.why: Contributions come out before net pay, so the gross/net distinction explains the first paycheck after enrolling.
The match formula and the vesting schedule are the two things on the form that are specific to your employer.
The form's Roth/traditional checkbox is a tax-timing choice, and this card explains what each box means.
The fee column on the fund menu is the one number known in advance.
Most 401(k) menus include one; this card explains what the name means.
The default option in many plans, and where fees most often hide.
Why the account's early years look slow and the late years don't.
